clue.text: Strange-sailor has come back to dance

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange

indicators.note: a sailor who has come back has turned round, so his letters are read backwards

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: An odd seaman has returned home to take to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Strange-sailor' tempts you to read one figure; split it into an adjective and a seaman, and 'come back' turns the seaman round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom step with swaying hips, one of the Latin dances.

clue.text: Stagger to bed in worst possible condition

parts.note: to rock is to sway or stagger
the bed of a river or sea is its bottom

explanation.surface: Someone lurching off to sleep in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' looks like somewhere to sleep, but it is a seabed or riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for the lowest point anyone can sink to.

clue.text: Chap with a little wood from swamp tree

parts.note: a chap is a man
a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: A man carrying some timber out of the swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical trees growing in coastal marshes on stilt-like roots.

clue.text: A maxim about soldiers and Cupid

indicators.note: the maxim goes about, that is around, the soldiers

parts.note: a maxim is a motto or saying
RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A soldierly saying set alongside the god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian term for a little Cupid, a cherub figure in art.

clue.text: Sees how the church is divided

explanation.surface: Observes the way a congregation splits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sees' looks like a verb but is the plural of see, a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is his district, and the church is split into these districts.

clue.text: Presumably not working clothes?

explanation.surface: Garments one does not wear to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working clothes' looks like one phrase; split it into two senses of the same slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a failure or faulty item is a dud, and old informal usage calls garments duds.

clue.text: Free kick in embarrassing position

explanation.surface: A football award won in an awkward spot.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a dead-ball kick taken from the flag, and to be in a tight spot is idiomatically to be cornered.

clue.text: Reason to upset foreign lady

indicators.note: upsetting the word means knocking its letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Grounds for annoying a woman from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish title for a married woman, equivalent to madam.

clue.text: Attempt to find house in street

indicators.note: the house is placed in the street

explanation.surface: Looking for a home somewhere along a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go at something is having a try or crack.

clue.text: Prisoner experienced defeat

parts.note: a con is a convict
found, as in 'found it hard', means experienced

explanation.surface: A convict who had already known failure.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart or overthrow, as in confounding one's enemies.

clue.text: Finish letters, perhaps, for waymarker

parts.note: to sign off is to finish, and a sign is a signature finishing a letter
letters are one example of post or mail

explanation.surface: Signing off correspondence, with a nod to route markers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish letters' reads as completing correspondence; really it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole bearing pointing arms that show walkers the way.

clue.text: To break the law is popular over the border

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits over, above, the other

parts.note: something in is fashionable or popular
a fringe is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Lawbreaking is the fashion on the far side of the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate a rule or right, contravening it.

clue.text: One needing a lift from the gym

definitions.text: One needing a lift from the gym

parts.words: One needing a lift from the gym
parts.note: sounds like a tired athlete wanting a ride home, but describes a weight that must be raised

explanation.surface: A worn-out exerciser hoping for a ride home.
explanation.definitionFit: A weightlifting bar with discs at each end, raised by gym users.

clue.text: Insolence over criticism of cosmetic

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits over, above, the other

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk or insolence
stick, as in 'took some stick', is criticism

explanation.surface: Backchat about someone's make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up applied to colour the mouth.

clue.text: In stronghold, captive man who's spilling the beans

indicators.note: the stronghold holds the man captive inside it

parts.note: a fort is a stronghold
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a fortress is telling all.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who passes secrets to police, a grass or snitch.

clue.text: I was sixty a long time ago

definitions.text: I was sixty a long time ago

parts.words: I was sixty a long time ago
parts.note: reads as an old person's remark, but describes an old-fashioned way of saying sixty, a count in twenties

explanation.surface: An elderly person recalling passing a birthday milestone long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty; the biblical phrase for a lifespan is three twenties and ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic number: three twenties make sixty.

clue.text: Athletics race so slippery, but there's no danger

indicators.note: slippery letters slide about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A track event so slick, yet safe enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom saying it is safe to proceed unobserved.

clue.text: Polite Scotsman, but he's not serving

parts.note: civil means courteous or polite
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A courteous Scot who has no military role.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone outside the armed forces, not in uniform.

clue.text: Interpreter of power symbol

explanation.surface: A translator of the emblem of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: An expounder of an idea or art, and in maths the superscript index showing a power.

clue.text: Girl said to be offering reservation

indicators.note: the word for girl is spoken, so only its sound counts

parts.note: miss is a girl or young woman
giving means offering

explanation.surface: A young woman reportedly being generous, with doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' applies only to the girl: the extra S of her title is lost when spoken, while 'offering' is taken as plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubt or qualm, as in having reservations.

clue.text: Cylinder of parchment, say, with list of names

explanation.surface: A rolled document bearing a register.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled-up writing sheet, and a roster or roll of honour.

clue.text: Albino's confession may transfix

parts.note: an albino might admit 'I am pale', contracted to I'M
the second half of the admission is the colourless word for white-faced

explanation.surface: Someone lacking pigment admits something that could pierce.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the confession as two words: I'M then PALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce through with a spike, pinning in place.

clue.text: Periodically, they're in charge

parts.note: seems to say people take turns in authority, but means those in charge of periodicals

explanation.surface: Managers who take charge from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but it means 'of periodicals'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of magazines and newspapers who decide what is published.

clue.text: Go to fish, using toll road

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
a pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Heading off to go fishing by paying highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic name for a road with a gate where fees were paid.

clue.text: Cut down to size?

parts.note: suggests humbling someone, but literally means shortening slightly to the right size

explanation.surface: Putting someone in their place.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipping hair or hedges slightly to neaten them.

clue.text: Simple point, but say in complicated way

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: the word is put in a complicated way, its letters tangled

explanation.surface: Something plain expressed in convoluted terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in complicated way' makes ASY from SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Straightforward, not difficult.

clue.text: Unattractive leading character ruined another one

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ugly protagonist spoils a second one.
explanation.definitionFit: A central figure in fiction lacking heroic virtues.

clue.text: Wartime port children danced round

explanation.surface: A wartime harbour that youngsters circled in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Second World War had floating harbours of this name; the nursery rhyme goes 'Here we go round the ___ bush'.
explanation.definitionFit: Name of the prefabricated D-Day harbours, and the bush in the nursery-rhyme dance.

clue.text: Explosive substance mistakenly taken as inert

indicators.note: the letters are taken mistakenly, in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A blasting compound wrongly thought to be harmless.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, used in gunpowder.
